item.title: 01 - Custom Buildroot Image running on RAM
item.description:
Introduction

My first goal is to have a working system running from RAM with a fixed IP address and an SSH server.

Building the Buildroot default configuration

As I am using the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, I will first build the default Raspberry Pi image that comes with Buildroot. For that, I will download Buildroot and choose the default configuration. I recommend taking a look at the Buildroot User Manual so you install the necessary dependencies.

item.title: Import raw images into LXD
item.description:
Introduction

Sometimes I want to quickly test simple things on raw images, and using LXD is a convenient way. This post documents how to import a raw Ubuntu Core image so you can test it.

Importing

LXD needs at least two files: your image in qcow2 format and a metadata file (in a tar file). I will be using the Ubuntu Core 26 image as an example.
